catalog_quote: Gruzdeva 1997 §2.1.2: "Ударение разноместное и подвижное. Может выполнять смыслоразличительную функцию: ҳáунт 'называет/называл' - ҳаýнт 'сушит/сушил'. Некоторые морфемы, при помощи которых образуются формы слов, всегда являются ударными. Это, например, показатели императива у глагола: ви-йá 'иди', ви-вэ́ 'идите', и суффикс звательной формы у имени существительного: ымык-á 'мать' (обращение). В одних и тех же словах в различных диалектах ударение иногда не совпадает: áмамд' (амур.) - амáмнт (вост-сахал.) 'ходит/ходил пешком'. Высказывается гипотеза о существовании в Н.я. тоновых противопоставлений." Fortescue 2016: 6 (archive.org scanned): "Stress in simplex words today is largely on the first syllable in A, though this is not always so. Krejnovié (1979: 298) sees it as “mobile”, thus for example whereas transitive bisyllabic words are stressed on the second syllable (in ES at least), corre…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations are verbatim in the held files at the stated locators (Gruzdeva 1997 §2.1.2, l.354-362; Fortescue 2016 p. 6, l.356-361; Shiraishi 2006 fn. 11 l.491). (2) Deciding source is a 1997 16-pp Jazyki-mira sketch by the leading specialist, pan-Nivkh but citing an ES form, backed second-hand by Krejnovich 1979: 298; consistent, specialist, but short. Glottolog lists no grammar for sakh1247; the one phonology monograph for a sakh1247 variety (Hattori 1962, fetched sources from the Hokkaido Univ. of Education repository) is segmental only. Web/API search (CrossRef, Glottolog family bibliography of 91 items, Shiraishi's publication list, KU ScholarWorks, VJa archive) found no instrumental or dedicated synchronic study of ES stress; Halm & Slater 2020 call Nivkh stress 'very understudied'. Shiraishi, Hidetoshi. 2002. Metrical evidence for cliticization in Nivkh pronouns. Ms., 27 pp. (author's site, ext-web.edu.sgu.ac.jp/hidetos/HTML/)
sources.quote: 'It is generally accepted that accent is placed on the leftmost syllable in Nivkh (Austerlitz 1956: 263, Bondarko and Zinder 1962: 85, Panfilov 1962: 21-22, Hattori 1988: 1409). Assuming from this observation that the language's metrical pattern is left-to-right trochaic ...'; accent shifts one syllable right off an epenthetic vowel in pronoun+bound-allomorph complexes. Data are Amur dialect, so not sakh1247; but two of the cited authorities (Austerlitz, Hattori) worked on SE Sakhalin (South Sakhalin dialect of sakh1247).
sources.locator: p. 10-11 (txt lines 641-677); data note fn. 1 (Amur-dialect speakers, Okha/Nogliki/Nekrasovka 2000-01)

sources.citation: Bondarko, L. V. & L. R. Zinder. 1962. Fonetičeskaja xarakteristika različnyx tipov sintaksičeskix sočetanij v nivxskom jazyke. Voprosy jazykoznanija 1962(4): 84-89.
sources.quote: Instrumental (oscillograph) study of intensity and vowel duration in object+verb and attributive complexes vs free phrases; five speakers all 'nositeli amurskogo dialekta'. Shows the verb loses intensity/duration after a direct object (one phonetic peak per complex). Says nothing about the syllable position of word stress and nothing about Sakhalin varieties.
sources.locator: pp. 84-89, esp. fn. 5 p. 84 (speakers) and p. 85

sources.note: The only article devoted to Nivkh accent (abstract seen: accent place in Proto-Nivkh 'depended on vowel height and syllable structure'; unstressed-vowel loss post-dates the Amur/Sakhalin split); it must tabulate Amur vs Sakhalin stress correspondences and would test whether ES stress is really free/lexical or (partly) predictable — our LEXICAL coding rests on a five-sentence pan-Nivkh sketch paragraph.
